A migration template (Microsoft Excel XML Spreadsheet 2003 file) consists of different sheets which are visible at the bottom of the migration template. You use the different sheets to specify the data that belongs to different data structures. For example the migration template for the migration object 'Product', contains a sheet for basic data, a sheet for plant data, and so on. Some sheets are mandatory, and some are optional.

A migration template is based on the active view of the relevant migration object. You can find information about the active view in the Microsoft Excel XML file. In the file, navigate to File -> Info. You can find the active view name under Properties -> Tags.

In the Microsoft Excel XML Spreadsheet 2003 file, navigate to 'File' -> 'Options' -> 'Advanced'. Under the option 'When calculating this workbook:', ensure that the option 'Set precision as displayed' is selected.

If you are migrating data to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, the default size limit for each uploaded XML file is 100MB. If required, you can zip several files together. Note that the combined size of all the XML files you want to add to the zip file must not exceed 160MB. The limit for zip file is still 100MB.
If you are migrating data to SAP S/4HANA, the default size limit for each uploaded XML file is 100MB.

You can increase the size limit for each uploaded XML file to 160MB by changing the system parameter (icm/HTTP/max_request_size_KB). If required, you can zip several files together. Note that the combined size of all the XML files you want to add to the zip file must not exceed 160MB. The limit for the zip file is still 160 MB with the adjusted system parameter.
The 'Field List' sheet is one of the first sheets in the migration template. You use this sheet to get an overview of the expected data in one central location.
It contains information about the mandatory and optional sheets, as well as detailed information for each sheet (for example the expected data type and length for the fields in each sheet).
On the 'Field List' sheet, you can view the following information for each field in the migration template:
• The name of the sheet, and whether it is mandatory or optional. Only mandatory sheets have the suffix 'Mandatory', for example 'Basic Data (Mandatory)'. All other sheets are optional.

You can quickly get an overview of the mandatory and optional sheets by looking at the color of the sheet names at the bottom of the migration template. The name of the mandatory sheets have the color orange, while the optional sheets have the color blue.
• The group name for the fields in a sheet.
• The individual fields in each sheet, as well as whether fields are mandatory for a sheet.
• Information about the expected format of the individual fields, for example the data type and length.

In the field list sheet, certain technical information about the fields is hidden by default. The columns 'SAP Structure' and 'SAP Field' (columns 8 and 9) are hidden by default. The column 'SAP Structure' is the technical name of the structure that the field belongs to. The column 'SAP Field' is the technical name of the field. To unhide these columns, select the columns adjacent to either side of the columns that you want to unhide. Right-click your selection, and choose 'Unhide'.

If you want to extract data from SAP ERP, the technical name of structure and the technical name of the field often corresponds to the SAP ERP table name and field name. Also, the SAP Release Note (2568909) for SAP S/4HANA Cloud data migration content uses the technical names of the structures and fields.
For each migration template, you need to specify data for the mandatory sheets, and for the optional sheets that are relevant for your project:
Mandatory sheets represent the minimum set of data you must provide for data migration. Fill in all mandatory fields.
Use optional sheets depending on your migration scope and available legacy data.
Viewing Additional Information for Each Column

In row 8, you can view the field names in SAP S/4HANA, as well as additional information such as the expected format (for example the data type and length). Note that you must expand the row to view this additional information.
Some fields are mandatory, and some are optional. The wildcard character (‘*’) beside the name of a field indicates that the field is mandatory.
Although an optional sheet may contain mandatory columns, if the sheet is not relevant for your project, there is no need to fill the mandatory columns in the sheet with data.

Rows 4, 5, and 6 are hidden by default. Row 4 is the technical name of the structure (corresponds to the sheet name). Row 5 is the technical name of the field (corresponds to row 8 - the field description). Row 6 contains technical information such as the data type and length.
To unhide these rows, select the rows adjacent to either side of the rows that you want to unhide. Right-click your selection, and choose 'Unhide'.
You can view the data type for a field in row 8 (see 'Viewing Additional Information for Each Column' above). Depending on the field, one of the following data types may be required:

Letters, numbers, and special characters are permitted. In the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit, you can map the values of certain fields with the data type text (usually those fields with Length: 80) to their correct SAP S/4HANA target values. You can do this value mapping in the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit when you start the transfer (in the step 'Convert Values').

Enter numbers with decimals in the relevant country-specific format, for example 12.34 (United States) or 12,34 (Germany). For fields with decimals, the declared length includes decimals (if required), for example if the information for the column states: Length: 8, Decimals: 3, then a number such as 12345.678 is permitted. Note that decimal places are not mandatory. In this example, you can specify a whole number up to length 8 without decimal places, for example ‘1’. This number would be set to ‘1.000’ internally. For negative numbers, ensure that a minus sign ('-') directly precedes the number, for example '-100'. Note that currencies with more than 3 decimal places are not supported.
Note that the maximum field length supported by Microsoft Excel is 15 digits (including decimals). If you have longer numbers, use the option for transferring data to S/4HANA using staging tables.

Enter the date in your country-specific format, for example 12/31/1998 (United States) or 31.12.1998 (Germany). Note that Microsoft Excel automatically recognizes different date formats and transforms them automatically to the correct XML format.
Enter the time in the format HH:MM:SS, for example 02:52:40

When copying data to a sheet from Microsoft Excel, always right-click the relevant cell and choose the paste option 'Values (V)'. Avoid pasting data that includes formatting and formulas into the migration template, as this will corrupt the structure of the XML migration template.
Using the Find and Replace Function

Do not use the Microsoft Excel function 'Find and Replace'. If you change data by using this function, you may also unintentionally change the field names and corrupt the structure of the XML migration template.
Ensure that you only save the migration template as a Microsoft Excel XML Spreadsheet 2003 file. Other file types are not supported by the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit.
Do not make any changes to the structure of the migration template, specifically:
• Do not delete, rename or change the order of any sheet in the migration template.
• Do not change the formatting of any cells.
• Do not hide, remove, or change the order of any of the columns in the migration template.
Any changes to the sheets will result in a corrupted XML structure. Such modified migration templates are not supported by the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit.

Plant Key uniquely identifying a plant. In Logistics a plant is an organizational unit for dividing an enterprise according to production, procurement, maintenance, and products planning. Type: Text Length: 80 *

MRP Type Key that determines whether and how the product is planned. This field becomes mandatory if MRP data should be migrated. Depending on the MRP type other fields are becomming mandatory eg if you choose 'VB' for reorder-point planning you also have to specify the Reorder Point, MRP controller, Lot Sizing Procedure ... Type: Text Length: 80
MRP Controller Specifies the number of the MRP controller or group of MRP controllers responsible for product planning for the product. Type: Text Length: 80

MRP Group The MRP group contains all the products from the point of view of MRP for assigning special control parameters for the total planning run. These control parameters include, for example, the strategy group, the consumption mode, and the planning horizon. Type: Text Length: 80

Reorder Point For MRP Type 'VB' (Reorder-Point-Planning) you have to specify the reorder point for reorder planning. In this case this field becomes mandatory. If the stock falls below this quantity, the system flags the product for requirements planning. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3

Planning Time Fence The planning fence time becomes required if you are working with MRP type which includes a firming type. This is for example the case for MRP type P1-P4 (Forecast Consumption, Auto/Manual Firming). The planning time fence specifies a period within which no automatic changes are to be made to the master plan. The planning time fence is maintained in workdays. Type: Number Length: 3
Planning Cycle Key that determines the day on which the product is planned and ordered. Type: Text Length: 80
Lot Sizing Procedure Key that determines which lot-sizing procedure the system uses within products planning to calculate the quantity to be procured or produced. Type: Text Length: 80
Minimum Lot Size Minimum procurement quantity. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3
Maximum Lot Size Quantity that is not allowed to be exceeded during procurement. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3

Fixed Lot Size Please enter a value if you are working with Lot Sizing Procedure 'Fixed order quantity'. The fixed lot size is then a required field. Note: In this case entries in fields: Minimum Lot Size, Maximum Lot Size and Rounding value will be reset. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3
Storage Cost Indicator Indicator that specifies the storage costs percentage the system uses when calculating the lot size to determine storage costs. Type: Text Length: 80

Lot Size Independent Cost Costs that are incurred, irrespective of lot size, for each purchase order or production order over and above the purchase order price or production costs. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 2
Currency for Lot Size Ind. Cost You must specify the currency for the Lot Size Independent Cost (currency of the company code belonging to the plant). Type: Text Length: 80

Assembly Scrap (%) Percentage scrap that occurs during production of the product if the product is an assembly. The assembly scrap is used in products planning to calculate the lot size of the assembly. The system increases the quantity to be produced by the scrap quantity calculated. Type: Number Length: 5 Decimal: 2

Maximum Stock Level Quantity of the product in this plant that may not be exceeded. In products planning, the maximum stock level is used only if you have chosen Replenish to maximum stock level as the lot-sizing procedure; that is, you have entered HB as the lot size key. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3
Rounding Value Value to a multiple of which the system rounds up the procurement quantity. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3

Takt Time If a requirement quantity (for example, for capacity reasons) cannot be procured in a single lot, you have to schedule several receipts. In conjunction with the overlap indicator in the lot size, you can use the takt time to specify that these receipts are offset, that is, that they are delayed by the takt time. You enter the takt time in workdays. Type: Number Length: 3
Rounding Profile Key that the system uses to adjust the order proposal quantity to deliverable units. Type: Text Length: 80
Safety Stock Specifies the quantity whose purpose is to satisfy unexpectedly high demand in the coverage period. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3
Service Level Warehouse Percentage specifying what proportion of the requirement is to be covered by the warehouse stock. Type: Number Length: 3 Decimal: 1

Coverage Profile The range of coverage profile contains the parameters for calculating the dynamic safety stock. This is a statistical calculation on the basis of average daily requirements. Type: Text Length: 80

Safety Time Indicator You use this indicator to switch on the safety time actual range of coverage for a product in MRP. If you define a safety time, the requirements in MRP are brought forward on the time axis by the number of workdays you define here. The actual range of coverage corresponds to the number of days, by which the requirements are brought forward. Using this indicator you can activate the safety time and you can set whether all requirements or only independent requirements (sales order, planned independent requirements, and so on) are to be brought forward. Type: Text Length: 80

Safety Time (in Workdays) In this field, you define the number of workdays for the safety time/actual range of coverage. If you define a safety time, the requirements in MRP are brought forward on the time axis by the number of workdays you define here. Type: Number Length: 2

Safety Time Period Profile The period profile for the safety time / actual range of coverage contains the periods (stating to/from date) with the safety time/actual range of coverage that is valid for each period. Type: Text Length: 80

MRP Relevancy for Dep. Requirements MRP relevancy (Materials Requirements Planning) for dependent requirements: This indicator controls whether dependent requirements are relevant to MRP or not. Dependent requirements include dependent reservations and stock transfer requirements. You only use this indicator in connection with planning strategies for make-to-stock production, assembly planning. Type: Text Length: 80
MRP Safety Stock Method The MRP Safety Stock Method provides different options to introduce a safety buffer. Type: Text Length: 80

Special Procurement Type The special procurement type is used to precisely define how in-house production and external procurement is to be carried out. Example: Special Procurement for External Procurement can be Consignment, Subcontracting ... Type: Text Length: 80

Default Storage Loc. for Ext. Proc. Default storage location for external procurement. Storage location that is proposed in the purchase requisition in products planning for subsequent storage of the product. In the case of a product procured externally, this storage location is proposed in the planned order in products planning. Type: Text Length: 80
Planning Calendar Three character number (numeric or using letters) that specifically identifies a PPS-planning calendar. Type: Text Length: 80

Consider Planned Delivery Time This is an indicator field. If you use Planned Delivery Time of the MRP Area, enter X. If you use Planned Delivery Time of the Plant, leave the field empty. Type: Text Length: 1
Planned Delivery Time Number of calendar days needed to obtain the product or service if it is procured externally. Type: Number Length: 3

Issue Storage Location Default storage location for produced inhouse. In the case of a product produced in-house, this is the key of the storage location that is copied to the planned order, production order, or run schedule quantity. If the product is a component, it is the issuing storage location to which a backflush is posted. Type: Text Length: 80

PP Planning Procedure Defines for each planning-relevant event that can occur for a location product, which action is executed by Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (PP/DS) in SAP APO if this event occurs. Type: Text Length: 80
Planning Package This field displays the planning package to which the location product belongs. Type: Text Length: 80
Lot Size Unit (ISO Format) Indicates the valid unit of measure of lot size. Type: Text Length: 80
Target Stock Level Method The Target Stock Level Method is used in production planning and detailed scheduling. Type: Text Length: 80

Target Days' Supply Target Days' Supply in Workdays. Enter the value for this field in the "HHMMSS" (hours, minutes, seconds) format. Example: For 3 workdays, enter 720000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 3.5 workdays, enter 840000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 150 workdays, enter 36000000 (HHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 9999 workdays, enter 2399760000 (HHHHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, sec.); this is the maximum field length for hours). Type: Number Length: 11

Reorder Days' Supply Reorder Days' Supply in Workdays. Enter the value for this field in the "HHMMSS" (hours, minutes, seconds) format. Example: For 3 workdays, enter 720000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 3.5 workdays, enter 840000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 150 workdays, enter 36000000 (HHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 9999 workdays, enter 2399760000 (HHHHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, sec.); this is the maximum field length for hours). Type: Number Length: 11
Period Lot Sizing Planning Calendar For the periodic lot-sizing procedure, use an APO standard time stream as a planning calendar. Type: Text Length: 10

Goods Receipt Processing Time The time between the delivery or the production of a product and its availability as stock. This time is used, for example, as handling time or time for quality checks, and is added to the transportation duration or the production time of a product. Enter the value for this field in the "HHMMSS" (hours, minutes, seconds) format. Example: For 3 workdays, enter 720000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 3.5 workdays, enter 840000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 150 workdays, enter 36000000 (HHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 9999 workdays, enter 2399760000 (HHHHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, sec.); this is the maximum field length for hours). Type: Number Length: 11

GR Handling Capacity Bucket Consumption Used by the Heuristic and Optimizer to calculate how much handling resource capacity is consumed by the product for a particular plan. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3
UoM:Handling Capacity in GR (ISO Format) Type: Text Length: 80

Goods Issue Processing Time The time between issuing the product from storage and transporting it. This time is used as handling time or time for quality control, and is added to the transport duration (Supply Network Planning and PP/DS) of a product. Enter the value for this field in the "HHMMSS" (hours, minutes, seconds) format. Example: For 3 workdays, enter 720000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 3.5 workdays, enter 840000 (HHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 150 workdays, enter 36000000 (HHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, seconds). For 9999 workdays, enter 2399760000 (HHHHHHMMSS – hours, minutes, sec.); this is the maximum field length for hours). Type: Number Length: 11

GI Handling Capacity Bucket Consumption Used by the Heuristic and Optimizer to calculate how much handling resource capacity is consumed by the product for a particular plan. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 3
UoM:Handling Capacity in GI (ISO Format) Type: Text Length: 80
Safety Stock Method Method for Calculating Safety Stock. Type: Text Length: 80

Safety Stock Method Determination This is an indicator field. If the criterion is met, enter X. If not, leave the field empty. 'X' = Safety Stock Method is Automatically determined. ' ' = Safety Stock Method is not Automatically determined. Type: Text Length: 1
Period Factor Factor used by the system to calculate the availability date/time of a receipt element within a time period (bucket). Type: Number Length: 4 Decimal: 3
Use Period Factor You use this indicator to define how the system determines the desired availability date/time of the receipts that should cover the requirements in a period. Type: Text Length: 1

Period Factor TDS Period Factor for Time-dependent Stock Levels is the factor used by the system to calculate the validity time of changes applied to time-dependent stock levels within a day. Type: Number Length: 4 Decimal: 3

Valuation Area Valuation area is the organizational level at which the product is valuated. Type: Text Length: 80 *

Valuation Type This is a further subdivision of the valuation category. The valuation category defines the valuation types allowed for a product. If a product is valuated by origin (for example, valuation category H), you can define the possible countries of origin as valuation types. For valuation category 'Single batch Valuation' you have to provide for each batch an own valuation type with the detailed price information. Further information can be found the migration object documentation under Mapping instructions - Single Batch Valuation and Split Valuation. Type: Text Length: 80
Price Control Determination The Price determination indicator determines whether price determination is: •Transaction-based •Single-level / multilevel Type: Text Length: 80

Valuation Class Assignment of a product to a group of G/L accounts With other factors, the valuation class determines the G/L accounts that are updated as a result of a valuation-relevant transaction or event such as a goods movement. The valuation class makes it possible to: •Post the stock values of products of the same product type to different G/L accounts •Post the stock values of products of different product types to the same G/L account Type: Text Length: 80 *

Valuation Class for Sales Order Default value for the valuation class for valuated sales order stocks of the product. You need specify a valuation class here only if you want to assign a different valuation class to this type of stock than that assigned to other valuated stocks of the product. This makes it possible to define other allowed G/L accounts for these stocks. Type: Text Length: 80

Valuation Class for Project Stock Default value for the valuation class for valuated project stocks of the product. You need specify a valuation class here only if you want to assign a different valuation class to this type of stock than that assigned to other valuated stocks of the product. This makes it possible to define other allowed G/L accounts for these stocks. Type: Text Length: 80

Currency You must specify the company code currency belonging to the valuation area. Type: Text Length: 80 *

Inventory Price Moving Average Moving average price if the product has price control indicator 'V' for moving average price. It changes the price with each valuation-relevant movement. Type: Number Length: 13 Decimal: 2

Inventory Price Standard Price Standard price of the product if the product has price control indicator 'S' for standard price. LIFO Pool Alphanumeric key uniquely identifying the document. Products to be valuated together are grouped under a pool number. Type: Text Length: 80
Devaluation Indicator A devaluation indicator representing the number of years a product has already been classed as "slow or non-moving". Type: Number Length: 2

Usage of the Product Use for BRAZIL only ! This indicator shows the intended usage of a particular product in inventory. Please note that each usage of a product must have a separate valuation. Product-Related Origin This is an indicator field. If the criterion is met, enter X. If not, leave the field empty. If this indicator is set, the product number will be written to the cost element itemization in the Controlling module. Type: Text Length: 80
With Qty Structure This is an indicator field. If the criterion is met, enter X. If not, leave the field empty. Type: Text Length: 1
Overhead Group Key that groups products to which the same overhead is applied. Type: Text Length: 80
